# AGENTS.md — GitHub Actions

Run jobs on Windows runners (`windows-*` labels) under native `pwsh`. Native Windows pull-request jobs live in `ci-windows.yml` and Python pull-request jobs in `ci-python.yml`, so each PR workflow can be re-run independently; their checks feed the required `windows checks passed` and `python checks passed` verdicts, as Linux jobs in `ci.yml` feed `all checks passed`; Wine runs Windows Node on hosted Linux only in `ci-master.yml`. Python runtime CI checks Linux/Windows x64 on pull requests and Linux ARM64 plus both macOS architectures on master pushes; releases retain all five targets ([platform policy](workflows/ci-master.yml)). `ci.yml`, `ci-windows.yml`, and `ci-python.yml` are pull-request-only. Master-only platform checks and manual runner benchmarks live in `ci-master.yml`, which listens to master pushes and `workflow_dispatch`, not `pull_request`; separating workflow triggers keeps master-only jobs out of PR check panels.

Pull-request Linux lanes (`node 24 / static`, coverage, lint, snapshots and artifacts), the verdict job, filename checks, and the sandbox `bwrap` leg use `ubuntu-latest`. Benchmarks use `ubuntu-24.04`. The sandbox matrix also uses `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, and `macos-latest`. Native Windows lanes and manual Windows packaging use `windows-latest`. Manual macOS packaging uses `macos-latest`. Python builder targets keep native GitHub-hosted labels: `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-latest`, `macos-15-intel`, and `windows-2025`. Both packaging workflows upload installer artifacts. These lanes use GitHub-hosted runners only: do not retarget them to Blacksmith, `dsh-*` labels, or self-hosted pools.

The merge checks run from three workflows named `Policy`, which run on `pull_request_target` so their definitions come from master, and call the `deepseek-harness-check` action directly: `pr-check-on-head-branch.yml` on pull-request updates gives `Policy / Master Change` and `Policy / Pre-Merge Check`, `pr-check-after-approve.yml` on pull-request updates and submitted or dismissed reviews gives `Policy / Approve Check` and `Policy / Reviewer Evaluate`, and `pr-check-on-base-branch.yml` on master pushes re-runs the head-branch checks as `Policy / Recheck`. Branch rules require those check names, so keep the job names and the workflow name. Each check reads its mode from a repository variable: `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF`, `MERGE_POLICY_PRE_MERGE`, `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF`, and `MERGE_POLICY_REVIEW`, each `off` (skip), `report` (run without failing the job), or `block` (fail the job); a missing value or an unknown one counts as `report`. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` merges the commit `Policy / Master Change` reports, so it runs only after that job and stays off while `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF` is `off`; a merge it cannot do and a build that fails both follow its own mode, so `report` warns and skips the build while `block` fails the job. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` runs `scripts/pre-merge-check.ts` under plain Node and knows nothing else about the merged tree: that script checks the released manifests against the root version, installs, and builds the Host and Client contracts, so change it in one pull request together with the build it orchestrates.
